summary: techportal 4.0.11 exfiltrates installer identifiers via preinstall beacon to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint with DNS fallback
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node beacon.js'. On npm install, beacon.js collects the installer's hostname, OS username, cwd, INIT_CWD, a stable context id, runtime signature, CI-provider code, and per-run event id, base32-encodes them into X-Bug-Bounty-* headers, and issues an HTTP GET to a hardcoded bare-IP callback at http://45.76.249.245/beacon/.../techportal/4.0.11. On HTTP failure, timeout, or non-2xx response, the same identifiers are encoded into DNS subdomain labels and resolved against seven probe domains under oob.asm5.net (a DNS out-of-band exfiltration channel that bypasses HTTP egress filtering). The package manifest self-labels as a 'controlled dependency-confusion proof' targeting the internal name 'techportal', but the beacon fires unconditionally on any install and any organization whose internal build accidentally resolves this public name has its internal host/user/path metadata shipped to a third party without consent.
